2027-04-08.title: Thursday of the Second Week of Easter
readings: We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit
The Lord hears the cry of the poor (or: Alleluia)
The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands
2027-04-08.alt: Easter weekday of the Second Week of Easter. The Alleluia is sung before the Gospel; the Regina Caeli replaces the Angelus until Pentecost. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-04-08.verse: He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.
theo: The apostles, brought back from the Temple, stand before the council. The high priest reminds them: “We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name.” He will not even say the name of Jesus. Peter and the apostles answer with a sentence that has given courage to believers in every century: “We must obey God rather than any human authority.” This is not a contempt for authority, which the apostles will later teach Christians to respect; it is the freedom of conscience before God when a human command forbids what God commands. Then Peter proclaims the Easter message once more: “The God of our ancestors raised up Jesus… God exalted him at his right hand as Leader and Savior that he might give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.” Notice the purpose of his preaching: not accusation but forgiveness, offered first to Israel, the people of the promise. The Church teaches that the responsibility for the Passion cannot be laid on the Jews of that time as a whole, still less on the Jews of today, and that all of us sinners share in it (Catechism 597–598). And Peter adds a second witness beside the apostles: “And we are witnesses to these things, and so is the Holy Spirit whom God has given to those who obey him.” The Spirit does not replace our witness; he speaks with it.

The Gospel closes the third chapter of St John with a meditation on the one who comes from above. John the Baptist has just said that he must decrease; now the evangelist explains why. “The one who comes from above is above all.” He does not speak second-hand; “he testifies to what he has seen and heard.” Whoever accepts his testimony “has certified this, that God is true,” like a man who puts his seal on a document. Then a phrase of great richness: “He whom God has sent speaks the words of God, for he gives the Spirit without measure.” The prophets received the Spirit by measure, for a time and a task; the Son receives and gives him without limit. “The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands.” Everything the Father has is in the hands that were pierced and are now risen. The chapter ends with a choice: “Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life.” The apostles in the council are living that choice. They have believed, they have received the Spirit, and so, before a powerful court, they can speak the words of God.
outline: Ask: when did you last have to choose between pleasing people and pleasing God?
Point 1 · Obey God rather than men
Conscience and courage before the council.
All things in the Son's hands.
“We must obey God rather than any human authority.”
live: Where you are tempted today to stay silent about what is right, say one clear and gentle word of truth.
Pray the Come, Holy Spirit each morning between now and Pentecost.
2027-04-08.prayer: God of our ancestors, you raised up Jesus and exalted him at your right hand as Leader and Saviour. Give us the courage of the apostles to obey you rather than any human voice that would silence your truth, and pour out on us without measure the Spirit of your Son, that we may be faithful witnesses of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Father has placed all things in the Son's hands, and in the Eucharist those risen hands give us his very self. The Spirit called down on the gifts makes them his Body and Blood, and makes us his witnesses.

quick: Before the council the apostles said: we must obey God rather than any human authority.
Peter preached that God raised Jesus to give repentance and forgiveness of sins.
Jesus speaks the words of God and gives the Spirit without measure; the Father has placed all things in his hands.
2027-04-08.action: Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” once this morning and once this evening, asking for courage to witness.
2027-04-08.question: Is there a place in my life where I keep quiet about Jesus because I fear what others will think?

family.explain: The leaders told the apostles: stop talking about Jesus! But Peter said: we must obey God first. God raised Jesus from the dead, and we have seen him. The Holy Spirit makes us brave to tell everyone.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in countries where it is dangerous to speak about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard to do what God wants, and who can help us?”

illus: A young accountant in a firm in Kochi was asked by his manager to change some figures before an audit. He was newly married and could not afford to lose his job. He asked for one night to think, prayed in front of the Blessed Sacrament at a city church, and the next morning told his manager respectfully that he could not do it. The manager was angry, but the audit found the original figures correct. Two years later, when the firm was investigated, his name was the only one nobody questioned.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, given without measure, fill us with courage and with love, and make us witnesses of the risen Lord. Alleluia. Amen.
share: We must obey God rather than any human authority (Acts 5:29). Where do I face a choice like this?
That he might give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins (Acts 5:31). Do I carry Easter as a message of forgiveness or of blame?
He gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:34). Do I ask for the Spirit generously or timidly?
pm.resp: The Lord hears the cry of the poor.
interc: For Christians under pressure to deny their faith, that the Spirit may give them courage.
For all in authority, that they may respect conscience and serve the truth.
For friendship and respect between Christians and the Jewish people.
For those who must choose between their job and their conscience.
For our group, that we may be witnesses together with the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you have placed all things in your Son's hands. Give us his Spirit and make us faithful witnesses. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the apostles stand before the most powerful court in their nation. They are told: stop teaching in this name. And Peter says: we must obey God rather than any human authority (Acts 5:29). These are not proud words. These are the words of a man who once denied Jesus out of fear, and who has now been changed by the Resurrection and the Spirit.

And what does Peter preach to his judges? Not anger. He says God raised Jesus to give repentance and forgiveness of sins. Even to those who opposed him, the risen Lord offers mercy. The Easter message is never a weapon against anyone; it is a door opened to everyone.

Peter says one more thing: we are witnesses, and so is the Holy Spirit. We are never alone when we speak of Jesus. In the Gospel John says that Jesus gives the Spirit without measure (John 3:34). He does not give the Spirit with a teaspoon. He pours him out.

So let us ask today for that Spirit. In our offices, our schools, our families, there are moments when we must choose between what people want and what God wants. Let us ask for the courage of Peter, and the gentleness of Peter too, so that our witness may be both firm and kind. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, the leaders told Peter: stop talking about Jesus! Peter was not afraid any more, because the Holy Spirit made him brave. He said: we must obey God first. When someone asks you to do something wrong, you can say: I want to obey God. The Holy Spirit will help you!

intro: Theme: “We must obey God rather than any human authority.”
Courage before the council, witnesses with the Spirit, and the Son who gives the Spirit without measure.

q: If I say, “I will not mention him, or speak any more in his name,” then within me there is something like a burning fire shut up in my bones; I am weary with holding it in, and I cannot.
But Peter and the apostles answered, “We must obey God rather than any human authority.”
points.apply: Form your conscience this week: read one page of the Catechism on a moral question you face at work or at home.

sub: Two witnesses: the apostles and the Spirit.
q: You are my witnesses, says the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he.
And we are witnesses to these things, and so is the Holy Spirit whom God has given to those who obey him.
points.apply: Tell one person this week, simply and without arguing, what the risen Jesus has done for you.

sub: Setting a seal to God's truth.
q: The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
The Father loves the Son and has placed all things in his hands.
points.apply: Put one worry into the hands of the risen Lord each night this week, naming it aloud in prayer.

concl: The Resurrection made the apostles bold and fearless before the council.
The Son who has all things in his hands gives the Spirit without measure to make us witnesses.
2027-04-08.resolve: Pray the Come, Holy Spirit every morning until Pentecost.
